questions.q: What does "living off the land" mean in the context of an attack?
options: Using legitimate, pre-installed system tools to carry out malicious actions instead of introducing custom malware
Burying malware inside image files to hide it from users
Attacking only agricultural or farming-industry networks
Running an attack exclusively from a physically unplugged machine
questions.explain: Living off the land means repurposing tools that are already legitimately installed, rather than bringing in new custom malware.

questions.q: Why do attackers favor LOLBins over custom malware?
options: The tools are already present, already signed, and already expected to run, so signature-based scanners have nothing new to flag
LOLBins are faster at encrypting files than custom ransomware
LOLBins can only be detected by antivirus, never by EDR
Microsoft specifically designs these tools to help attackers
questions.explain: Because these binaries were already on disk and signed before the attack began, there's no new file for a signature scanner to catch.

questions.q: What is certutil.exe's real/documented purpose, and what capability do attackers abuse?
options: It's a certificate-management utility; attackers abuse its ability to download files from a URL and decode base64 data
It's a backup utility; attackers abuse its ability to encrypt entire drives
It's a remote desktop tool; attackers abuse its ability to capture keystrokes
It's a firewall configuration tool; attackers abuse its ability to disable all rules
questions.explain: certutil is officially for certificate management, but it has a long-documented side ability to download and base64-decode files that has nothing to do with certificates.

questions.q: Why can't signature-based antivirus catch a living-off-the-land technique?
options: Every binary involved is a legitimate, already-signed file already on disk, so there's no new file to hash or match against a signature database
Signature-based antivirus has been fully replaced by EDR in every modern environment
Living-off-the-land techniques only occur on Linux, where antivirus doesn't run
The tools involved are always encrypted, making scanning impossible
questions.explain: From a file-scanning point of view, certutil.exe running is certutil.exe running, regardless of who invoked it — there's nothing new to flag.

questions.q: What actually distinguishes a legitimate admin's use of a LOLBin from an attacker's use of the same tool?
options: Command-line arguments, process lineage, and context such as who is running it and when, not the identity of the file itself
The version number of the operating system
Whether the tool was downloaded from the internet or came preinstalled
Nothing — legitimate and malicious use are indistinguishable even to EDR
questions.explain: Behavioral signals — the specific command-line pattern, the lineage leading up to it, and the surrounding context — are what EDR rules actually key on, since the file itself gives no answer.
